content: Keep the desktop UI's established look, which the user approved on 2026-10-08. It has a navy brand header (--brand #1f3a5f), a light canvas (#f2f4f7) with white panels, an 8px radius, and Segoe UI text with Cascadia Mono for code. The results list sits on the left (20–26rem) and the part detail on the right. The window itself never scrolls; only panels and columns do. Inside the part detail, a header sits on top. Below it, the symbol and footprint are stacked on the left and share the height, and every catalog field is always visible on the right, with no collapsible. Long URL values stay on one line with an ellipsis. Symbols render on KiCad's light schematic paper and footprints on KiCad's dark board (#001023). Each error state has one alert, and supporting notes stay quiet. Reuse the tokens in apps/desktop-ui/styles.css rather than adding colours, and extend this layout rather than redesigning it.

title: Sign in to the team catalog with an in-memory session, loopback only for now
rationale: The desktop saves only the team server address and email (config/team.json); the password is sent once to auth-with-password and the session token stays in memory, so nothing secret is stored and a restart asks for the password again. Only http://127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] are accepted because collaboration's realtime client speaks plain HTTP and a password must not cross a network unencrypted; a shared server needs HTTPS realtime first. Edit access is the users field can_edit_catalog, which members cannot set on themselves.

description: A component class with display:flex (.team-tabs) overrode the HTML hidden attribute, so tabs meant to hide behind the conflict view stayed visible; the journey's el.hidden check still passed.
resolution: styles.css ends with [hidden] { display: none !important; }. Journey 06 checks layout (getClientRects().length === 0), not the hidden property.

description: In Leptos 0.8.3, calling .track() on a Memo inside an Effect did not re-run the Effect when the memo's source changed (the search did not refresh after a team Change), while .get() on an equivalent memo elsewhere worked.
resolution: Read the memo's value in the Effect (let _ = memo.get();) instead of only tracking it; .track() is fine on RwSignals (apps/desktop-ui/src/main.rs search effect).

title: The team column shows shared part details and the current revision apart; one Edit part form
rationale: Seed kicad-parts-7556, chosen for the simplest product without asking the user (who asked for best judgement). Details tab: 'Part details (N)' with the hint 'Every revision of the part shares these details.', then manufacturer parts, then 'Symbol and footprint (revision N)'. No separate list of other revisions: the history already lists every revision. One 'Edit part' button and form (not two): fieldsets 'Part details', 'Manufacturer parts', and 'Symbol and footprint' with the hint 'Changing these adds a revision after revision N. Designs that use an earlier revision keep it.'; the form starts with 'Change details only to correct them. A part with a different value, package or pinout needs a new IPN.' Save notices: 'Saved. The part details changed; no revision was added.' or 'Saved as revision N.' History: one entry per Change, titled 'Part details · Edited by X' or 'Revision N · Imported by an administrator', (current) on the entry that added the current revision; the selected entry shows 'What changed in revision N' or 'What changed in the part details' with Before/After rows (details rows first). Conflict screen: 'X saved a change on <time> (reason) after you started editing.' with columns Field / You started from / Theirs / Yours; only the sections that moved conflict. Deliberate simplification: the conflict screen keeps one heading ('Someone else changed this part first') and one table for both sections, while the behaviour stays per section (only rows of what moved or what you changed appear, and saving on top resends only the sections you changed). Revision wording: the part's own revision says 'revision N of this part' (Details heading, header Source fact), a CAD item's says 'symbol revision N' or 'footprint revision N' (binding rows, preview notes), so the two never read alike. The header's Source fact stays 'Team catalog, revision N'. Styles reuse existing tokens; the only new rule is .team-toolbar + .hint { margin: 0 0 0.5rem }.
